author: porteratzo
body:
### Integration of Hippmapp3r Model Training into openfl-security

#### Overview
This PR integrates the Hippmapp3r medical segmentation model into the openfl framework. It enables users to call the `keras/hippmapp3r` model using the command `fx workspace create --template keras/hippmapp3r`. The primary focus of this PR is to test the functionality of the Hippmapp3r model, training it on random synthetic data.

#### Key Features
1. **Model Integration**: 
   - The Hippmapp3r model is now part of the openfl-security framework.
   - Users can initiate the model training with the specified template.

2. **Synthetic Data Generation**:
   - Synthetic data is generated using `setup_data.py`.
   - The amount of synthetic data can be adjusted by modifying the `required_file_size_MB` parameter in the `setup_data.py` file.

3. **Model Configuration and Weights**:
   - The task runner downloads the model configuration and weights from Google Drive.
   - It verifies the hash to ensure data integrity before loading the model.

#### Testing
- The primary objective of this PR is to validate the functionality of the Hippmapp3r model.
- The model will be trained on randomly generated synthetic data to ensure proper integration and performance.

#### Usage
To use the Hippmapp3r model with openfl-security, run the following command:
```command line
fx workspace create --template keras/hippmapp3r
```

#### Notes
- Ensure that the `required_file_size_MB` parameter in `setup_data.py` is set according to your data requirements.
- The model configuration and weights are securely downloaded and verified for integrity.<!-- ##StartCodeSummary## -->

author: renaynay
body:
This PR introduces several changes, but namely fixes fee estimation according to the [ADR](https://github.com/celestiaorg/celestia-node/pull/4048/files). Now, blob transactions will estimate gas price in the case that the user did not specify a gas price.

Other changes: 
* the code related to the estimator has been removed from node. Now node simply wraps the app's `TxClient` methods and does some simple sanity checks on the TxConfig to ensure the `gasPrice` and `gasUsage` are to the user's expectations (if specified via TxConfig)
* There is no more looping through grpc connections to perform gas price / usage estimation. If an estimator service address is provided via the `state` config's `EstimatorAddress` field, or via the flag `--estimator.service.address`, a gRPC connection to that address will be initiated/managed by the node and will be passed to the `TxClient` for it to use for gas price/usage estimation *exclusively*. There is *no fallback* to using the default core connection provided to the TxClient. We have deliberately made the failure of the estimator service explicit here. 
* There are now only two methods exposed to us via `TxClient`: `EstimateGasPrice` and `EstimateGasPriceAndUsage`. The former will be used for blob txs as we can estimate gas via an algorithm on the node side (no tx simulation required) and the latter will be used for all other tx types.
* I have removed code related to querying the minimum gas price as we now use gas price estimation for better tx submission. Even if an estimator address is not provided, the default core endpoint that the node is configured with can still be used for gas price estimation. 
* `SubmitPayForBlob` will no longer perform retries.

**Harfbuzz 11.0.0:**

What's Changed
- There are three new font-functions implementations (integrations) in this release: hb-coretext has gained one, calling into the CoreText library, hb-directwrite has gained one, calling into the DirectWrite library. hb-fontations has gained one, calling into the Skrifa Rust library.
- All three are mostly useful for performance and correctness testing, but some clients might find them useful.
- An API is added to use them from a single API by providing a backend name string: hb_font_set_funcs_using()
- Several new APIs are added, to load a font-face using different "face-loaders", and a single entry point to them all using a loader name string: hb_ft_face_create_from_file_or_fail() and hb_ft_face_create_from_blob_or_fail() hb_coretext_face_create_from_file_or_fail() and hb_coretext_face_create_from_blob_or_fail() hb_directwrite_face_create_from_file_or_fail() and hb_directwrite_face_create_from_blob_or_fail() hb_face_create_from_file_or_fail_using()

- Several performance optimizations have been implemented.
- Application of the trak table during shaping has been improved.
- The directwrite shaper now supports font variations, and correctly applies user features.
- The hb-directwrite API and shaper has graduated from experimental.
- Various bug fixes and other improvements.

body:
This pull request introduces a significant refactor to make scheduler configuration values dynamically configurable through environment variables. The changes include creating a new `Config` struct to hold configuration values, updating various functions to use these new configuration values, and adding utility functions to load configuration from environment variables.

Key changes include:

Configuration Management:
* Added `Config` struct to hold configuration values (`KVCacheThreshold`, `QueueThresholdCritical`, `QueueingThresholdLoRA`, `LoraAffinityThreshold`) and initialized it using environment variables (`pkg/epp/scheduling/scheduler.go`).
* Implemented utility functions `getEnvFloat` and `getEnvInt` to retrieve configuration values from environment variables with default fallbacks (`pkg/epp/scheduling/scheduler.go`).

Function Updates:
* Updated `leastQueuingFilterFunc` and `loRASoftAffinityFilter` to use the new configuration values (`pkg/epp/scheduling/filter.go`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-39a77c3f30c969fdb254c6c00de96eb242c30bb66489d56fc572b9e549c97363L144-R144) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-39a77c3f30c969fdb254c6c00de96eb242c30bb66489d56fc572b9e549c97363L226-R226)

Testing Enhancements:
* Modified `TestLoRASoftAffinityDistribution` to set and restore configuration values for testing purposes (`pkg/epp/scheduling/filter_test.go`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-96eede232beb0e3f1b04523a8f9c3e5e4f8db91ec3037e3f96bc6344d9c18ff5R445-R456) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-96eede232beb0e3f1b04523a8f9c3e5e4f8db91ec3037e3f96bc6344d9c18ff5L475-R490) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-96eede232beb0e3f1b04523a8f9c3e5e4f8db91ec3037e3f96bc6344d9c18ff5L505-R523)

body:
Having `contents: write` permission in an action can be risky as any supply-chain issues can then modify the workflow.

If the xml files are not actually needed in the repository then using these changes will allow them to still be published to github pages without committing them to the repository.

If merged then the repo settings need to be modified to publish the github action instead of the branch:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1bd0fc6b-2a61-4793-a1ef-cdc0caa7b5f0)

The commit also creates a `_site` directory, downloads to there, and only publishes that directory. This means currently published URLs like https://simonw.github.io/ollama-models-atom-feed/README.md will no longer be available. If that's a problem just remove the `mkdir/cd` lines.

The changes follow the [starter-workflows for pages](https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows/blob/main/pages/static.yml). Similar changes may want to be made to the template repo.

1. 절차식 → 객체지향 → 함수형 프로그램으로 패러다임이 변화했다. , 변화란 이전의 문제점을 개선하기 위해 등장하는데, 절차식에서 객체지향으로 오면서, 데이터와 함수를 하나의 객체로 관리하면서 절차적 언어의 코드 재사용성과 유지보수를 개선했다. 그런데 객체지향에서 함수형 프로그램으로 왔을 때는? 그 목적이 무엇이었을까? 불편함 개선? 함수를 변수로 넘길 수 있게 되면서 간단 명료한 코드가 되지만? 더 있을거 같은데 모르겠다. 
2. 객체지향도 낮설었지만, 함수형 프로그램은 허허… 눈에 익히고, 손에 익힐 수 밖에 없다. 

## 💡 배운 점

함수형 프로그래밍을 배우면서 객체지향 프로그래밍의 문제점을 이해할 수 있었다. 객체지향 프로그래밍은 상태 변화, 강한 결합, 동시성 문제와 같은 한계를 가진다. 반면, 함수형 프로그래밍은 불변성, 작은 단위의 함수 조합, 멀티스레드 환경에서의 안정성을 통해 이러한 문제를 해결한다. 따라서 어느 한 방식이 무조건 더 좋은 것이 아니라, 두 개념이 서로 보완적인 관계임을 알게 되었다.

## 🔄 자체 평가 & 회고

체력이 떨어져 힘이들지만...  이해 없이 나아가는것이 더 힘들다. 시간이 들더라도 찾아보자

body:
## Overview

This PR implements a decentralized system for tracking, verifying, and marketing heritage grain varieties using Clarity smart contracts on the Stacks blockchain. The system enables small-scale farmers to register traditional grain varieties, document growing protocols, verify seed purity, and connect directly with specialty markets.

## Components

### Smart Contracts

1. **Variety Registration Contract** (`variety-registration.clar`)

1. Records details of traditional grain types
2. Tracks heritage status and origin information
3. Allows retrieval of variety details



2. **Growing Protocol Contract** (`growing-protocol.clar`)

1. Documents cultivation practices for specific varieties
2. Stores planting and harvesting guidelines
3. Links protocols to specific grain varieties



3. **Seed Purity Verification Contract** (`seed-purity-verification.clar`)

1. Tracks genetic integrity of heritage grains
2. Manages seed batch registration and certification
3. Maintains chain of custody for seed lineage



4. **Direct Market Contract** (`direct-market.clar`)

1. Facilitates connections with specialty bakers and brewers
2. Manages listings, orders, and feedback
3. Enables direct farmer-to-buyer transactions





### Tests

Comprehensive test suite using Vitest:

- `variety-registration.test.ts`
- `growing-protocol.test.ts`
- `seed-purity-verification.test.ts`
- `direct-market.test.ts`
- `test-utils.ts` (shared testing utilities)


## Implementation Details

### Design Decisions

1. **Simplified Data Structures**

1. Focused on essential fields to reduce complexity
2. Used standard Clarity maps for data storage
3. Implemented simple ID-based retrieval patterns



2. **Independent Contracts**

1. Each contract operates independently to reduce dependencies
2. Contracts can be deployed and used separately
3. Manual verification of relationships between entities



3. **Security Considerations**

1. Owner-based permission checks for updates
2. Certification requirements for marketplace participation
3. Validation of inputs to prevent invalid data





### Key Features

1. **Variety Registration**

1. Register heritage grain varieties with origin information
2. Retrieve variety details by ID



2. **Growing Protocol Documentation**

1. Create standardized growing protocols for specific varieties
2. Document planting and harvesting guidelines



3. **Seed Batch Certification**

1. Register seed batches with variety information
2. Simple certification process for seed purity



4. **Direct Market Connection**

1. Create and manage listings for certified grain batches
2. Update listing details and status





## Testing Strategy

The test suite verifies:

- Basic creation/registration functions for all entities
- Retrieval of entity details
- Update operations with permission checks
- Error handling for invalid operations


Tests use mock implementations of Clarity contracts to simulate blockchain behavior without requiring a full deployment.

## Future Enhancements

Potential improvements for future PRs:

1. **Cross-Contract Integration**

1. Implement proper cross-contract calls for entity verification
2. Add contract references for more robust data validation



2. **Enhanced Verification**

1. More detailed seed purity testing and verification
2. Integration with external testing authorities



3. **Advanced Market Features**

1. Escrow functionality for transactions
2. Reputation system for farmers and buyers
3. Auction mechanisms for rare varieties



4. **Data Analytics**

1. Tracking of growing conditions and yield data
2. Performance comparisons across different protocols





## How to Test

1. Run the test suite:

```plaintext
npm test
```


2. Manual testing steps:

1. Deploy contracts to Clarinet or a testnet
2. Register a sample variety
3. Create a growing protocol for the variety
4. Register and certify a seed batch
5. Create a market listing for the batch





## Related Issues

This PR addresses the need for a transparent, verifiable system for heritage grain production that:

- Preserves agricultural biodiversity
- Creates value for small-scale farmers
- Ensures authenticity for specialty buyers
- Facilitates knowledge sharing about traditional varieties

body:
This PR is a significant cleanup and reworking of the native QUDA accessors.
* Data ordering changes
  * Gone are explicit `FLOAT2`, `FLOAT4`, `FLOAT8` data orderings, we now just have `NATIVE` ordering
  * The data ordering is now set for all fields by `CMake` parameters
    * `QUDA_ORDER_DOUBLE`, `QUDA_ORDER_SINGLE`, `QUDA_ORDER_HALF`, `QUDA_ORDER_QUARTER`
    * The values of these correspond to the inner vector length desired, e.g., 4 would be a `FLOAT4` accessor
  * For fields, whose degrees of freedom are not a multiple of the vector length we deal with the remainder explicitly
    * E.g., for a SU(3) field with 18 real numbers, and a `FLOAT4` accessor, we would have 4x `FLOAT4` ld/st instructions and a 1x `FLOAT2` remainder.
  * Vector lengths 2, 4, 8, and 16 are supported (up to 256-bit in total length)
* Add support for shared-memory carve out autotuning
  * Enabled with the environment variable `QUDA_ENABLE_TUNING_SHARED_CARVE_OUT=1`
* Adds explicit support for Blackwell (sm_100)
* Adds support for future-looking optimization
  * Shared-memory spilling can be opted into on a per-kernel basis
  * Maximum register cap can be opted into on a pre-kernel basis
  * `SharedMemoryCache` can use a warp stride layout which transforms all index offsets into immediate (disabled by for now)
* The CMake parameter `QUDA_ALTERNATIVE_I_TO_F` is now a numerical value between 0 and 100 in units of 25.  This indicates the percentage of instructions that go through the alternative path instead of using conventional conversion.  Default remains at 0 (= OFF previously).
* Fix some warnings in nvc++ 

The effect of the changes in this PR is to significantly improve performance for the stencil kernels on Blackwell, and some modest improvements on Hopper.

author: hubert-reinterpretcast
body:
`env -u` is not supported by the system `env` utility on AIX.
`/opt/freeware/bin/env` is the standard path for the GNU coreutils `env` utility as distributed by the AIX Toolbox for Open Source Software.
Adding `/opt/freeware/bin` to `PATH` causes issues by picking up other utilities that are less capable, in an AIX context, than the system ones.
This patch modifies the relevant usage of `env` to use (on AIX) the full path to `/opt/freeware/bin/env`.

author: htyu
body:
Enable a third warp group to do the epilog job:
```

Barrier p[3],c[3], tp[2], tc[2]

# Producer
if warp_id == [0,3]:  
  for k in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K), phase=1, idx=0):
     ProducerAcquire(c[idx], phase)
     a[idx] = tl._experimental_descriptor_load(a_ptrs, p[idx])
     b[idx] = tl._experimental_descriptor_load(b_ptrs, p[idx])     
     a_ptrs += BLOCK_K * stride_ak
     b_ptrs += BLOCK_K * stride_bk
     phase = (idx < 2) ? phase : phase ^ 1 
     idx = (idx + 1) % 3     

# MMA Consumer 
if warp_id == [4,7]:  
  ProducerAcquire(tc[outer_idx], outer_phase)
  tmem_store(c1[outer_idx], 0)
  for k in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K), phase=0, idx=0):
      ConsumerWait(p[idx], phase)
      c1 += tl.dot(a1[idx], b[idx], c[idx])
      phase = (idx < 2) ? phase : phase ^ 1
      idx = (idx + 1) % 3
  ProducerCommit(tp[outer_idx])

# Epilog Consumer
if warp_id == [8,11]:  
  ConsumerWait(tp[outer_idx], outer_phase)
  tmem_load
  ConsumerRelease(tc[outer_idx])
  c_ptrs = c_ptr + stride_cm …
  tl.store(c_ptrs, c1)
```

author: desrosj
body:
## Proposed changes

This implements the [recommendation to pin full length commit SHAs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions) instead of versions or branches when using 3rd-party GitHub Actions to protect from supply chain attacks.

This has been happening more often recently, with a number of popular actions having all of their tags updated with a buried vulnerability.

While the new notation is more verbose, a bit ugly, and requires every update to be applied manually, we can rely on Dependabot to handle that for us to make it more manageable.

No actual updates to actions are happening here. The latest versions correspond with the previous notation used.

Recent examples

Examples of actions being exploited in the wild:
- [changed-files](https://semgrep.dev/blog/2025/popular-github-action-tj-actionschanged-files-is-compromised/)
- [reviewdog's action library](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/reviewdog-github-actions-are-compromised)

#### Production

- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Dependency update
- [ ] Refactoring / housekeeping (changes to files not directly related to functionality)

#### Development

- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Dependency update
- [ ] Environment update / refactoring
- [ ] Documentation Update
- [X] Build/Test Tooling update

## Checklist

- [X] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/bluehost/.github/blob/master/.github/contributing.md) doc
- [ ] I have viewed my change in a web-browser
- [ ] Linting and tests pass locally with my changes
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [ ] I have added necessary documentation (if appropriate)

## Further comments

GitHub is [looking into providing immutable releases](https://github.com/features/preview/immutable-actions) for actions (which would allow versions to be used again), and this is currently in the [Q3 2025 roadmap](https://github.com/github/roadmap/issues/592). But we should use full SHA values until then.

See also https://github.com/newfold-labs/workflows/pull/22.

author: desrosj
body:
## Proposed changes

This implements the [recommendation to pin full length commit SHAs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions) instead of versions or branches when using 3rd-party GitHub Actions to protect from supply chain attacks.

This has been happening more often recently, with a number of popular actions having all of their tags updated with a buried vulnerability.

While the new notation is more verbose, a bit ugly, and requires every update to be applied manually, we can rely on Dependabot to handle that for us to make it more manageable.

No actual updates to actions are happening here. The latest versions correspond with the previous notation used.

Recent examples

Examples of actions being exploited in the wild:
- [changed-files](https://semgrep.dev/blog/2025/popular-github-action-tj-actionschanged-files-is-compromised/)
- [reviewdog's action library](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/reviewdog-github-actions-are-compromised)

#### Production

- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Dependency update
- [ ] Refactoring / housekeeping (changes to files not directly related to functionality)

#### Development

- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Dependency update
- [ ] Environment update / refactoring
- [ ] Documentation Update
- [X] Build/Test Tooling update

## Checklist

- [X] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/bluehost/.github/blob/master/.github/contributing.md) doc
- [ ] I have viewed my change in a web-browser
- [ ] Linting and tests pass locally with my changes
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [ ] I have added necessary documentation (if appropriate)

## Further comments

GitHub is [looking into providing immutable releases](https://github.com/features/preview/immutable-actions) for actions (which would allow versions to be used again), and this is currently in the [Q3 2025 roadmap](https://github.com/github/roadmap/issues/592). But we should use full SHA values until then.

See also https://github.com/newfold-labs/workflows/pull/22.

author: whatcookie
body:
Uses vpcompress to vectorize this otherwise unvectorizeable loop
the u16 path needs AVX-512-ICL because vpcompressw isn't included in skylake-x level AVX-512
the u32 path is untested as I couldn't find any games that hit it

We use vcompress register to register, rather than directly to memory since there's a bug with vcompress to memory on zen4, which makes it exceedingly slow. In the future, we could detect this and emit the optimal instructions in the jit instead. But the code is already so fast that it might not be worth the effort.

The code is overall nearly 10x faster than the scalar version on my zen4 machine.

body:
Added an optional field `point_id` to filter by. A single address can have multiple pickup points in the array `HentePunkts` and they can be far apart. At my home address there are 12(!) of them, so the data currently returned contains a lot of noise and does not accurately tell me when collection happens at my closest pickup point.

I also made `house_letter` optional as there is not always one and the API does not require it. Current behaviour is confusing as you're required to enter one, and I had to get around it by entering a space in that field.

Example of a API query for address with multiple pickup points:
https://www.oslo.kommune.no/xmlhttprequest.php?service=ren.search&street=N%C3%A5kkves%20vei&number=5&street_id=15280

Output of `test_sources.py -s oslokommune_no`:

```
Testing source oslokommune_no ...
  found 4 entries for Villa Paradiso
  found 1 entries for Nåkkves vei
```

author: desrosj
body:
## Proposed changes

This implements the [recommendation to pin full length commit SHAs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions) instead of versions or branches when using 3rd-party GitHub Actions to protect from supply chain attacks.

This has been happening more often recently, with a number of popular actions having all of their tags updated with a buried vulnerability.

While the new notation is more verbose, a bit ugly, and requires every update to be applied manually, we can rely on Dependabot to handle that for us to make it more manageable.

No actual updates to actions are happening here. The latest versions correspond with the previous notation used.

Recent examples

Examples of actions being exploited in the wild:
- [changed-files](https://semgrep.dev/blog/2025/popular-github-action-tj-actionschanged-files-is-compromised/)
- [reviewdog's action library](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/reviewdog-github-actions-are-compromised)

#### Production

- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Dependency update
- [ ] Refactoring / housekeeping (changes to files not directly related to functionality)

#### Development

- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Dependency update
- [ ] Environment update / refactoring
- [ ] Documentation Update
- [X] Build/Test Tooling update

## Checklist

- [X] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/bluehost/.github/blob/master/.github/contributing.md) doc
- [ ] I have viewed my change in a web-browser
- [ ] Linting and tests pass locally with my changes
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [ ] I have added necessary documentation (if appropriate)

## Further comments

GitHub is [looking into providing immutable releases](https://github.com/features/preview/immutable-actions) for actions (which would allow versions to be used again), and this is currently in the [Q3 2025 roadmap](https://github.com/github/roadmap/issues/592). But we should use full SHA values until then.

See also https://github.com/newfold-labs/workflows/pull/22.

author: njaecha
body:
## Changes/Fixes:
- Set SpriteMeshType to FullRect for a small performance improvement in the Picker Panel
- New nicer image for the button in studio
- Added option to toggle the clothing unlock
- Fixed issue with skirts that resulted in FK breaking

## Issues that I have found but wasn't able to fix:
-  Changing the hair in pseudo maker leaves back BoneInfos of the old hair part which cause Hair FK being unusable. These BoneInfos are sitting in at least three places: OCIChar.listBones, OCIChar.oiCharInfo.bones and Singleton<Info>.Instance.dicBoneInfo. Since it is normally not possible to change the hair of a character in Studio there is no code to clean up those BoneInfos. I have been unsuccessful in cleaning them, and the only way to use FK after changing the hair, is copy-pasting the character (which internally saves character into a buffer and then loads it from scratch).

body:
This PR adds a standalone web application script (`web_app.py`) for the EVE Online Market Bot. This allows users to run the web interface independently from the main script.

## Changes

- Added `web_app.py` - A standalone script that runs the web server with command line options for host, port, and debug mode
- Updated README.md to include information about the standalone web application and its usage

## Benefits

- Users can now run the web interface directly without having to use the main script
- The standalone script provides additional command line options for customizing the web server
- The web interface can be run independently from other bot functionality

## How to Use

```bash
# Run with default settings (host: 0.0.0.0, port: 5000)
python web_app.py

# Run on a specific host and port
python web_app.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

# Run in debug mode
python web_app.py --debug
```
